About the Work
My practice has evolved from incorporating mirrors to using abstract representations of water as a symbolic form of reflection.
Crys Adams · Artist Statement

In Sacral, the mirror that defined Adams's earlier work gives way to water. At the top of the panel a pair of cupped hands opens like an eye onto a reflective surface; below, a wave gathers and breaks across a burning horizon. A seam of gold runs between them — the language of kintsugi, in which what has been broken is repaired, and the repair is made the most luminous part of the whole.

Its title evokes the sacral — the body's seat of water, feeling, and creation. The painting holds the viewer at the threshold between surface and depth, asking not so much to be looked at as to be looked into.

Set within the mirror at its center, the viewer's own reflection enters the picture — and the work is completed only in the act of looking inward.
